subject: Customer-controlled edge maintenance -> SLA boundary / exception request
messages:
From: Tom Blake <tom.blake@luminahealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Zara Patel <zara.patel@luminahealth.com>
Date: Sun, 23 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: availability note — customer edge maintenance windows and attribution

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the quick onboarding last week. We're seeing periodic 4xx spikes from the private deployment in our telemetry that consistently line up with our scheduled WAN maintenance windows (weeknight router refreshes between 02:00-03:15). We understand Redwood's SLA expects availability for the Private deployment, but because these maintenance windows are fully controlled by our network team (edge routers and MPLS peering), we're asking whether Redwood can limit attribution for those intervals, or accept a scoped exception for the edge-maintenance periods.

If needed, we can provide network diagrams, scheduled maintenance CSVs, and sample packet captures. Our objective is to avoid an SLA breach on your side for events that originate on our bare-metal edge. What's the process to formalize this?

Tom
Sr. Infrastructure Manager
LuminaHealth

Attachments (listed): lumina_net_diagram.pdf (network diagram, 2 pages), scheduled_maintenance_windows.csv (list of recurring windows), sample_tcpdump_metadata.txt (pcap metadata only)
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Blake <tom.blake@luminahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: availability note — customer edge maintenance windows and attribution

Tom — thanks for the context and the attachments. This is exactly the sort of evidence we need to consider a bounded SLA attribution carve‑out.

High level: Redwood's Private SLA ties availability to the inference service and its managed dependencies. We do have procedures for handling customer-controlled infrastructure (edge, transit, customer KMS, etc.), but we need a concrete, auditable way to exclude short, documented maintenance windows from availability calculations. Practically, that looks like:

- A defined appendix to the Private SLA that lists recurring maintenance windows and the specific network domains / ASNs that are customer-controlled.
- Required evidence: scheduled maintenance CSV + network diagram + at least two weeks of correlating telemetry showing that client QPS drops are synchronous with the listed windows.
- Telemetry handoff: an agreed method to correlate Redwood's request timestamps with LuminaHealth's maintenance windows (UTC references), and a packet/flow-level sampling policy for spot checks.

Can you confirm the CSV cadence and whether the network diagram includes peering IP ranges and ASN tags? Also looping in Karthik and Soojin from our infra/legal ops side to outline the operational steps and legal language.

If you can confirm availability of the evidence and a sample two-week correlation window, we can draft an "Edge Maintenance Appendix" and run it through Legal for signature.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Head, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 14:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: availability note — customer edge maintenance windows and attribution

Tom / Zara — thank you for the files and the suggested delivery options. We've reviewed the CSV and diagram and had a short ops review with Karthik and Soojin. Summary and next steps below.

Decision: Redwood will provision a bounded "Edge Maintenance Appendix" to the Private SLA for LuminaHealth that limits SLA attribution for short, scheduled customer-controlled maintenance windows under the following conditions (draft summary):

1) Scope: Recurring maintenance windows up to 120 minutes in duration per occurrence, explicitly listed in the appendix by UTC time range and ASN/subnet scope. Non-recurring emergency maintenance is out of scope unless pre‑approved.

2) Evidence required: weekly CSV export (signed or S3-delivered), network diagram with ASNs & peering subnets, and at least two 14-day correlation windows where Redwood telemetry and LuminaHealth maintenance windows align. Packet capture metadata is acceptable in-lieu of full pcaps for privacy/compliance.

3) Telemetry correlation: Redwood will use request timestamps and regional routing metadata to map affected flows to the listed ASNs. If correlation exceeds the agreed confidence threshold (we'll define a >90% synchronous correlation for the first two windows), the corresponding downtime minutes shall be excluded from Redwood's SLA availability calculation.

4) Operational controls: LuminaHealth will provide an on-call contact for scheduled changes and commit to publishing the CSV at least 48 hours before a window change. Redwood will retain correlation logs for 90 days for dispute resolution.

5) Term & review: Appendix will apply for an initial 6-month term and will be reviewed at 90 days for efficacy. Either party can request adjustments with 30 days' notice.

Next steps (action items):
- Redwood (Karthik/Soojin): Draft the Edge Maintenance Appendix language and the telemetry correlation spec.
- LuminaHealth (Tom): Confirm whether you can automate CSV export + S3 token by Sep 10.
- Legal (Marcus): Prepare a short-form amendment template for signature once ops terms are nailed down.

I'll circulate the draft appendix by Sep 3. If that works for you, we can run it through Legal and finalize before the initial 6-month term starts.

Regards,
Naomi
Head, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
